criteria.description: Every component the description calls for (a step, group, input, output, decision, or repeated block, stated or directly implied) is visibly drawn, matched by meaning rather than exact wording, even if its label is imperfect. Components such a diagram typically shows but the description does not call for are noted, not scored. A component that cannot be made out because the image is too small or blurry is not counted here; it is scored under Legibility. Connections are judged under Connectivity, not here.

No drawn component is out of place: unrelated to what the description is about, duplicated by mistake, or contradicting the description. Additional detail that fits the described diagram (extra steps, sub-steps, counts, exclusion boxes) is fine. Titles, captions, legends, arrowheads, and container frames are not components.
Connected components follow one consistent reading direction, such as top-to-bottom or left-to-right. Connections that loop back to an earlier step are expected and are not violations.
Every drawn component and arrow stays fully inside the canvas; nothing is cut off at the edge.
No component unintentionally overlaps or collides with another; a container drawn around its members is allowed. Each colliding component counts once.
Arrows are routed cleanly: they do not pass through components or across text, cross other arrows only where unavoidable, and take no confusing detours.

Every connection the description calls for is drawn, directly or through intermediate drawn steps, in the right direction. A connection to a component that is not drawn is judged under Presence, not here.

Every drawn arrow is right: none points the wrong way, contradicts the described flow, connects parts that should not be connected, dangles with an end attached to nothing, or duplicates another arrow.

Each drawn component carries a meaningful label that names its role and agrees with the description (the exact name, where the description gives one), rather than a missing, generic, or placeholder label. Components that are not drawn are judged under Presence, and labels too small to read under Legibility.
Every drawn arrow that the description gives a label or condition, such as a YES/NO branch, shows that label correctly.
Text stays inside its box without clipping, and no text collides with other text.
Every label is large and clear enough to read at the size the diagram is displayed. A component too small or blurry to make out at all also fails here.
Text stands out clearly from its background; there is no light text on a light fill or dark text on a dark fill.
